q: SI Ramesh hears city student protest called national emergency and stops all bail production. Correct advice?
options: City protest alone triggers full emergency
Only war, external aggression or armed rebellion can trigger it
Any loud agitation triggers it after 1978
expl: 44th deleted internal disturbance; only war, external aggression, armed rebellion remain.
why: City protest is ordinary law-order under BNSS. Emergency needs grave national ground plus written Cabinet advice.

q: Constable asks if war rumour ends all fundamental protections. SHO should say?
options: All rights vanish in any emergency
Ban on retroactive punishment and life-liberty always remain
Police can force confessions in war
expl: Protections of Arts 20-21 are non-suspendable even in war emergency.
why: No torture or retrospective case is allowed ever. Production and humane custody continue for every SI.
trapnote: Half-truth: war affects some rights, not all.

q: During emergency for external attack, youth stopped for slogans. Which freedom affected without separate order?
options: Speech and assembly freedoms stand auto-suspended
expl: Art 19 auto-suspends only on war or external aggression ground.
why: External ground freezes 19 by Constitution force. Other rights need separate order and never include 20-21.
trapnote: Do not extend auto-rule to rebellion.

q: No Governor report but Delhi senses breakdown. Can President act?
options: Yes if otherwise satisfied of breakdown
expl: Proclamation can be on report or otherwise on satisfaction.
why: Otherwise allows central inputs. Report is one route, not the only route.

q: Treasury asks if pay-cut emergency was ever used. True position?
expl: Financial emergency under Art 360 never invoked in India.
why: No President has proclaimed it so far. Any past-use claim is false history.

q: Lok Sabha wants to end continuing national emergency against ministers wishes. Remedy?
options: Pass disapproval and President must revoke
expl: LS disapproval by simple majority compels revocation; special sitting on 1/10th notice.
why: 44th gave LS kill-switch. Once passed, revocation is mandatory not discretionary.

q: During armed rebellion emergency officer curbs press citing auto-ban. Correct?
options: No, auto-rule only for war/external aggression
expl: Armed rebellion does not trigger automatic Art 19 suspension.
why: Officer needs separate Presidential order. He cannot claim automatic freeze on rebellion ground.

q: Centre wants to dismiss ministry without floor test. Court law requires?
expl: Bommai 1994 mandates floor test; courts review mala fide.
why: Bommai made floor test compulsory. Dismissal without it is liable to be struck down.

q: Army curfew under military authority seeks cover for bona fide acts. Relevant idea?
options: Parliament may indemnify acts during martial law
expl: Art 34 lets Parliament indemnify acts to restore order under martial law.
why: Martial law is military rule distinct from emergency. Parliament can validate order-restoring acts.

q: Commandant bars jawans political union for discipline. Support?
options: Parliament may limit forces rights for discipline
Any officer may suspend at will
expl: Art 33 empowers Parliament to abridge forces/police rights for discipline.
why: Forces accept discipline curbs. Only Parliament makes that law, not executive order.

q: Compare approvals: national vs state emergency. Correct?
options: National special majority, state simple majority
expl: 352 needs special majority; 356 needs simple majority approval.
why: National is harder to approve. State follows simpler approval with time caps.

q: Compare caps: national vs President Rule. Correct?
options: National periodic renewal; President Rule max 3 years
expl: 352 extends every 6 months; 356 capped at 3 years.
why: National has no 3-year cap if approved. State cannot exceed 3 years.

q: Compare war vs rebellion rights effect. Correct?
options: War auto-affects speech; rebellion needs separate order
expl: Auto-suspension of 19 only on war/external aggression.
why: Ground matters. Rebellion leaves 19 intact unless separately suspended.

q: Compare martial law vs national emergency. Correct?
options: Martial law local military rule; emergency constitutional regime
Emergency means army courts replace all
expl: Martial law is area military authority; emergency is Union power.
why: They differ in scope. Indemnity for martial acts is separate from rights freeze.

q: Compare use history: financial vs others. Correct?
options: Financial never used; other two used
expl: 360 never invoked; 352 thrice, 356 over hundred times.
why: History shows varied use. 1991-use claim is classic distractor.

q: Statements: 1 Written Cabinet advice needed. 2 Internal disturbance still ground. 3 LS can compel revoke. Correct?
expl: Written advice and LS revoke true; internal disturbance deleted by 44th.
why: Statement 2 uses pre-1978 law. Statements 1 and 3 reflect post-44th safeguards.

q: Statements: 1 Speech auto-freezes in all emergencies. 2 Life-liberty never suspend. 3 Separate order for others. Correct?
expl: 20-21 immune; others need order; 19 auto only on war/external.
why: Statement 1 overgeneralises war rule. Statements 2 and 3 state precise scheme.

q: Statements: 1 Governor report compulsory. 2 Floor test mandatory. 3 Max 3 years. Correct?
expl: Report-or-otherwise; Bommai floor test; 3-year cap.
why: Statement 1 ignores otherwise route. Limits in 2 and 3 are settled law.

q: Statements: 1 Financial emergency in 1991. 2 Martial indemnity needs Parliament law. 3 Forces curbs by Parliament. Correct?
expl: 360 never used; 34 and 33 correctly stated in 2 and 3.
why: Statement 1 invents history. Statements 2 and 3 allocate power to Parliament alone.

q: Statements: 1 Oral nod enough. 2 Approval special majority. 3 Emergency always ends all rights. Correct?
expl: Written advice needed; special majority true; always false due 20-21.
why: Statement 1 fails written need. Statement 3 fails on always because 20-21 survive.
